# Hack Tracker

> A plain-English tracker of confirmed hacking incidents and outages people suspected were hacks. Official explanations and sources on every entry. Last updated 2026-11-21.

Site: https://hacktracking.com/

## Confirmed Hacks

Incidents confirmed by the affected organization, a government agency, or law enforcement. Most recent incident or news update first.

- [Infcurion Wallet Station (payment app platform, Japan; Payどん, AEON Pay)](https://hacktracking.com/#infcurion-wallet-station-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, High): Japanese fintech Infcurion says a third party broke into Wallet Station, the platform companies use to run their own smartphone payment apps, and personal data of app users leaked. It detected a flood of access on the night of Nov. 19, blocked the attacker's traffic, applied an emergency vulnerability patch and cut off service to the affected clients.
- [GL.iNet (router and KVM maker, cloud remote management)](https://hacktracking.com/#gl-inet-2026-11) (Nov 20, 2026, High): Router maker GL.iNet says an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management service and installed malicious software on a subset of its routers and KVM devices. It identified the problem on Nov. 20 and says it closed the hole in its cloud service.
- [MoEngage (customer engagement platform, India; ZebPay)](https://hacktracking.com/#moengage-2026-10) (Late Oct. 2026, Medium): Customer messaging platform MoEngage says that in late October an attacker used a compromised third-party vendor account to get into a limited part of its cloud infrastructure. It told customers about it in a Nov. 20 email and confirmed the breach on Nov. 21. Crypto exchange ZebPay told its users on Nov. 21 that information about some of them was taken from MoEngage.
- [YMCA of Singapore Youth For Causes portal](https://hacktracking.com/#ymca-of-singapore-youth-for-causes-portal-2026-10) (Oct 19, 2026, Low): YMCA of Singapore says the online application portal for its Youth For Causes programme and the associated database were hit by a cybersecurity breach. It was alerted on Oct. 19 and had the portal vendor take the system offline that day, then brought in forensic investigators. It told participants and mentors on Nov. 21.
- [ZOZO (ZOZOTOWN and WEAR, Japan, via PLAID KARTE)](https://hacktracking.com/#zozo-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, Critical): Japanese online fashion retailer ZOZO says data it kept in KARTE, the PLAID marketing service hacked on Nov. 13, leaked. PLAID's investigation showed on Nov. 15 that part of ZOZO's customer data had been taken from PLAID's databases; ZOZO announced it on Nov. 20.
- [PLAID KARTE customers (MUFG Bank, JINS, Shimamura and others, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#plaid-karte-customers-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, Critical): Attackers exploited a vulnerability in servers run by PLAID, the Tokyo company behind the KARTE customer-data marketing service, stole credentials used to connect to its systems and databases, and read data out. They also took over a PLAID account to get into the admin console. PLAID shut down all KARTE services on Nov. 13, and companies that use KARTE have been announcing leaks of their own customers' data since. On Nov. 20 PLAID said about 2,200 client companies in total (counting overlaps) had data leaked or possibly leaked.
- [Yumir Link Cuenote FC (email delivery service, Japan; Peach Aviation, JR Central and others)](https://hacktracking.com/#yumir-link-cuenote-fc-2026-10) (Oct 16, 2026, Critical): Tokyo-based Yumir Link found on Oct. 16 that attackers had broken into its Cuenote FC bulk email delivery service. It says they exploited a program vulnerability to steal its support staff's credentials, planted malicious programs on servers to pull data straight from databases, and hijacked logged-in customers' sessions to download address lists through the admin screen. Companies that send mail through Cuenote FC have been announcing leaks since late October.
- [Jeonju University (South Korea)](https://hacktracking.com/#jeonju-university-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): Jeonju University says its online liberal arts course service (AHA) was hacked at about 11:42 p.m. on Nov. 16. It confirmed the leak about 16 hours later, blocked outside access and reported it to regulators. It came a day after the Jeonbuk education office's school bus system breach.
- [Caring (senior care company, South Korea)](https://hacktracking.com/#caring-2026-08) (Aug 11, 2026, High): Senior care company Caring says an outside attacker bypassed authentication and got into an internal data lookup tool between Aug. 11 and Sept. 3. It closed the hole on Sept. 4 and at first thought no personal data was viewed, but a later review found the attacker had looked up records using existing accounts. It confirmed the leak on Nov. 17 and reported it to KISA.
- [Ransomware network extorting U.S. firms (Ukraine arrests)](https://hacktracking.com/#ransomware-network-extorting-u-s-firms-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, High): Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office, working with the FBI, said police arrested four suspected key members of a ransomware group of at least 27 people, part of a wider network of more than 60 that includes former Conti members. Police say the group posed as IT support to trick employees into handing over logins or installing remote access tools, then stole data and encrypted systems. Ukrainian authorities have since linked the four to the Chaos ransomware operation, which Computer Weekly reports grew out of the Royal/BlackSuit lineage; they are accused of a 2024 attack on Maxxis under the BlackSuit name before switching to Chaos.
- [Equinor (energy company, Norway)](https://hacktracking.com/#equinor-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): Norway's state-controlled oil and gas giant said it detected an ongoing cyberattack against some of its IT systems and was working to neutralise it.
- [Osaki Electric (smart meter maker, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#osaki-electric-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): Ransomware encrypted data on servers at Osaki Electric, a major Japanese maker of smart electricity meters. In a second report on Nov. 20 the company said the attacker most likely got in at about 1:30 a.m. on Nov. 15 by getting past the login on its VPN device, probably by trying passwords on an account that did not have multi-factor authentication, and then encrypted some virtual servers. It cut its systems off from outside networks on Nov. 17 and shut down production systems at its Saitama plant and two production subsidiaries.
- [Visa (via third-party provider)](https://hacktracking.com/#visa-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): A new ransomware gang called n0n listed Visa on its leak site and set a 48-hour deadline to publish data it claims to have stolen. Visa confirmed an incident, but says it started at an unnamed third-party service provider in the Asia Pacific region. On Nov. 19 the gang published a dataset tied to Visa's premium dining and loyalty programs in Asia-Pacific.
- [JPMorgan Chase (via third-party vendors)](https://hacktracking.com/#jpmorgan-chase-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, High): JPMorgan Chase said third parties that provide services to the bank were targeted in a cyberattack and that the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors. The ransomware gang n0n, which had listed the bank on its leak site, dumped data on Nov. 19 that Cybernews says is tied to the bank's invitation-only Reserve card program. BleepingComputer reports that n0n claimed an attack on cloud data analytics company Qubole on Nov. 11 and that Qubole is suspected to be the provider involved; JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard have not named it.
- [N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts (email security cloud)](https://hacktracking.com/#n-able-mail-assure-and-spamexperts-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): N-able said unknown attackers gained unauthorized access to a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud. A service disruption that started Nov. 16 was first traced to configuration and service dependencies, but the company later determined it was caused by the security incident and disabled management interfaces and APIs.
- [RIKEN Fugaku supercomputer (Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#riken-fugaku-supercomputer-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, High): An outsider broke into the internal network that runs Japan's Fugaku supercomputer through a public status dashboard, tampered with internal servers, and took or may have taken user data. RIKEN shut Fugaku down to contain it.
- [Japan Digital Agency government file-sharing service (GSS)](https://hacktracking.com/#japan-digital-agency-government-file-sharing-service-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, High): Japan's Digital Agency says someone other than the intended recipients accessed files on the file-sharing service in its Government Solution Service (GSS), which government agencies use to share large files such as meeting materials with each other and outside parties. It detected the access on Nov. 12, cut the service off from outside networks and stopped it.
- [European supermarket refrigeration systems (Delhaize, SuperValu, ICA and others)](https://hacktracking.com/#european-supermarket-refrigeration-systems-2026-11) (Nov 2, 2026, High): In the early hours of Nov. 2, a second wave of attacks hit internet-connected refrigeration controls at supermarkets and food businesses in at least 10 European countries, switching fridges and freezers into defrost mode. Around 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg and 13 SuperValu stores in Ireland were among those hit, and three British meat suppliers were affected through vulnerable Copeland XWEB controllers.
- [Leipzig University (Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#leipzig-university-2026-10) (Oct 28, 2026, High): Leipzig University's IT systems have been largely offline since a cyberattack on Oct. 28. On Nov. 20 the rector said forensic analysis found the attackers had reached 112 virtual servers that departments and institutes rent from the university computing center, for example for research projects.
- [U.S. Department of Agriculture applications](https://hacktracking.com/#u-s-department-of-agriculture-applications-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): Many USDA applications, including Farm Service Agency loan software, the NRCS ProTracts program that releases farmer payments, and other financial tools for farmers, were knocked offline for about a week. An internal USDA email reported by Nextgov/FCW said its security operations center "uncovered a security incident" that required resetting all database passwords and applications. On Nov. 20, Under Secretary of Agriculture Richard Fordyce told reporters the event was a "cyberthreat," not a "software update."
- [Eskenazi Health (Indianapolis public hospital system)](https://hacktracking.com/#eskenazi-health-2026-06) (Jun 3, 2026, High): Eskenazi Health, the public hospital division of the Health and Hospital Corporation of Marion County, announced that unauthorized individuals got into the cloud-based work accounts of some employees and accessed patients' electronic health information. Investigators believe the access began June 3; Eskenazi found and cut it off on July 27, Aug. 31 and Sept. 26.
- [GoFundMe Pro (nonprofit fundraising platform, Salesforce integration)](https://hacktracking.com/#gofundme-pro-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, High): GoFundMe says an unauthorized third party made repeated attempts to access GoFundMe Pro and was able to gain access to personal donor and supporter information. On Nov. 11 Salesforce disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app and managed packages after spotting suspicious use of access tokens tied to the provider; GoFundMe told customers the attacker accessed credentials for its Salesforce integration that may have been used to reach organizations' Salesforce records.
- [Revolve Group (online fashion retailer)](https://hacktracking.com/#revolve-group-2026-09) (Sep 11, 2026, High): Online fashion retailer Revolve, which runs Revolve.com and FWRD.com, told the SEC in an Oct. 29 filing that attackers got into several of its systems, including its online shopping platform, on Sept. 11 and used "automated means" to take customers' saved payment card details. A proposed class action filed Nov. 13 in federal court in Illinois says the breach affected about 1.5 million people.
- [Access Dental Management (dental service organization, Texas)](https://hacktracking.com/#access-dental-management-2026-05) (May 1, 2026, High): Irving, Texas-based Access Dental Management (ADM), which supports dental practices in Texas, Illinois, Indiana and New Mexico, says it discovered a cyber incident on May 5 and that hackers had accessed its network and viewed or copied data between May 1 and May 4. Its review of the affected files finished on Oct. 21, and it notified the Texas and Vermont attorneys general in November. The WorldLeaks extortion group claimed the attack on June 5; ADM has not commented on that claim.
- [POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology, South Korea)](https://hacktracking.com/#postech-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, Medium): South Korean research university POSTECH says an outside attacker exploited security flaws in its research equipment portal and IT service portal between 12:30 and 3:30 a.m. on Nov. 13, got administrator rights and viewed personal data. The break-in came to light while staff looked into an illegal cryptocurrency mining program found on a lab GPU server.
- [Kurly (online grocery, South Korea)](https://hacktracking.com/#kurly-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Korean online grocer Kurly says an outside attacker got into its systems on Nov. 17 by an abnormal method, stole authentication credentials and used them to reach internal business systems. It blocked the intrusion and reported it to authorities on Nov. 18.
- [Meta M (call center outsourcer, South Korea; Coinone, Bunjang, Mega MGC Coffee)](https://hacktracking.com/#meta-m-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Meta M, which runs customer service centers for about 150 companies, says an outside party broke into its systems early on Nov. 12, and phone numbers and counseling conversations were viewed or taken from some systems. Clients including crypto exchange Coinone, resale app Bunjang and Mega MGC Coffee have reported leaks.
- [Norwegian (airline website card skimming)](https://hacktracking.com/#norwegian-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): Norwegian says one of its external IT suppliers was hit by a cyberattack and malicious code was placed on parts of its website for a limited time on the afternoon and evening of Monday, Nov. 16. It found out on Nov. 18 and switched off the affected technology.
- [Canton of Basel-Country administration (Switzerland)](https://hacktracking.com/#canton-of-basel-country-administration-2026-11) (Nov 15, 2026, Medium): Unidentified attackers have been hitting the IT infrastructure of the Swiss canton of Basel-Country since Sunday, Nov. 15, the Cantonal Chancellery said. Some servers were cut off from the internet as a countermeasure. On Nov. 20 the canton said forensic analysis showed the attackers got into a database of work permits for cross-border commuters and stole data.
- [Monadnock Community Hospital (New Hampshire)](https://hacktracking.com/#monadnock-community-hospital-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, Medium): A systems outage at the Peterborough, N.H. hospital was caused by a cyber incident, hospital leadership said. Network disruptions were first detected on the afternoon of Nov. 8; phones and other systems went down and ambulances were diverted from the ER.
- [Charleston County Government (South Carolina)](https://hacktracking.com/#charleston-county-government-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): Charleston County's IT team spotted unusual network activity on Nov. 16 and the county has confirmed data was copied from its systems. The South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) has deemed the incident criminal and is assisting the investigation.
- [City of South Portland (Maine)](https://hacktracking.com/#city-of-south-portland-2026-11) (Nov 14, 2026, Medium): The city shut down its network after discovering a cybersecurity issue; its preliminary assessment points to cybercriminal activity.
- [New Zealand Defence Force websites (Force4Families discounts)](https://hacktracking.com/#new-zealand-defence-force-websites-2026-11) (Nov 20, 2026, Medium): The New Zealand Defence Force says its website provider notified it on the morning of Friday, Nov. 20 of unauthorized access to its website systems. It took the affected public websites offline and began a forensic investigation.
- [AMC Insurance Brokerage claims app AMC air (South Korea)](https://hacktracking.com/#amc-insurance-brokerage-claims-app-amc-air-2026-11) (Nov 5, 2026, Medium): Korean insurance broker AMC (에이엠씨손해보험중개) says outsiders downloaded insurance claim lists and member lists from its AMC air claims app between Nov. 5 and 15. It found the downloads during a security check on Nov. 18, shut the service down the same day and reported it to authorities.
- [Samsung Ads (via advertising data vendor, North America)](https://hacktracking.com/#samsung-ads-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Medium): The n0n ransomware gang dumped 220MB of data it claims belongs to Samsung on its leak site after its deadline ran out. Samsung confirmed a cyber incident at a third-party vendor that supported advertising data processing for its North America Service Business (Samsung Ads), and says the vendor's preliminary investigation indicates some Samsung information may have been affected.
- [RMS Cloud (hotel booking software, Australia)](https://hacktracking.com/#rms-cloud-2026-10) (Oct 26, 2026, Medium): Hotel and holiday park reservation software provider RMS says it found unauthorized access to a limited part of its environment on Oct. 26. Guests then got WhatsApp, text and email scams quoting their real booking details and asking for card payments.
- [Bookeasy (tourism booking platform, Australia; national park bookings)](https://hacktracking.com/#bookeasy-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, Medium): Bookeasy, which runs national park camping and permit bookings for Queensland, Victoria, South Australia and the ACT plus tourism sites like VisitCanberra, detected unauthorized activity on its platform. Park customers then received phishing emails and WhatsApp messages.
- [Bell Canada (telecom)](https://hacktracking.com/#bell-canada-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Bell confirmed that what it called an "agentic" threat actor got into some of its systems on Tuesday, Nov. 17, including one used for ordering and supplying telecommunication networks, and stole some enterprise (business) client data. Bell says it quickly contained the attack.
- [Culture Experience (TSUTAYA store operations, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#culture-experience-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, Medium): Culture Experience, which runs Japan's TSUTAYA bookstore and media chain business, said it found signs of unauthorized access by a third party to some systems in a data center it uses on Nov. 9 and cut those systems off from the data center. It announced the incident on Nov. 20.
- [AIRDO (airline, Japan, via email delivery provider)](https://hacktracking.com/#airdo-2026-10) (Oct 31, 2026, Medium): Hokkaido-based airline AIRDO said a third party broke into the outside email delivery system it used, and customers' email addresses leaked through emails sent via that system. It stopped using the system on Oct. 31 and has been switching to a different provider.
- [The Container Store (retailer)](https://hacktracking.com/#the-container-store-2026-11) (Nov 14, 2026, Medium): Parent company Neighborhood Intelligence said The Container Store restored its website and systems after a cybersecurity incident the previous weekend. Online ordering had been shut down, and stores stayed open using alternative transaction-processing procedures.
- [West Virginia Legislature](https://hacktracking.com/#west-virginia-legislature-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Medium): West Virginia's state legislature is responding to a cybersecurity incident that began Thursday, Nov. 19, took down its website and hit its IT systems. Outside cybersecurity specialists are helping contain and investigate it.
- [Chargemap (EV charging app, France)](https://hacktracking.com/#chargemap-2026-11) (Nov 8, 2026, Medium): Chargemap says an outside party exploited a security flaw in a legacy technical interface on Nov. 8 to extract user account data. It spotted abnormal activity on Nov. 10, fixed the flaw on Nov. 12 and notified France's data protection authority, the CNIL, on Nov. 13.
- [French precious-metals brokers and crypto tax service (10 charged)](https://hacktracking.com/#french-precious-metals-brokers-and-crypto-tax-service-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Medium): Paris prosecutors and France's gendarmerie said ten people were charged on Nov. 19 over the hacking of three precious-metals brokers and a company that helps people declare crypto holdings to tax authorities. Prosecutors say stolen customer data was used for targeted scams: "callers" urged victims to move funds or metals for safekeeping, and others went to victims' homes to collect physical assets.
- [Stolen U.S. government data seller "DP BRUCE" (arrest in Pakistan)](https://hacktracking.com/#stolen-u-s-government-data-seller-dp-bruce-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, Medium): Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency said it arrested a suspect in Karachi on Nov. 11 who allegedly used the alias "DP BRUCE" to advertise and sell stolen databases on the LeakBase forum and Telegram, taking payment in cryptocurrency.
- [Roll20 (online tabletop gaming platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#roll20-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): Roll20 says an unauthorized third party got into its systems on the evening of Nov. 16. According to the notification email as reported by PrivacyAffairs, the attacker exploited a vulnerability in a system that processed animated image uploads to reach records in a database of account information. Roll20 began emailing affected users on Nov. 20.
- [Onosys (restaurant online ordering platform; Dion's)](https://hacktracking.com/#onosys-2026-10) (Oct 10, 2026, Medium): Onosys, an Ohio company that runs online ordering for multi-unit restaurant chains, emailed customers on Nov. 18 that it found unusual activity on its ordering platform in October and that card details entered between Oct. 10 and 13 may have been accessed or captured by an unauthorized actor. New Mexico pizza chain Dion's confirmed its online customers were affected; in-person and phone orders were not.
- [Hugendubel and LovelyBooks (bookseller and reader network, Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#hugendubel-and-lovelybooks-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Medium): Munich bookseller Hugendubel and the reader social network LovelyBooks both said they were the target of a cyberattack overnight into Nov. 19. Hugendubel said its emergency plans kicked in and everything was taken offline.
- [East Asian universities (Cairn AI agent hacking campaign)](https://hacktracking.com/#east-asian-universities-2026-09) (Sep 8, 2026, Medium): Amazon Threat Intelligence says an attacker it assesses with moderate confidence to be Chinese-nexus used Cairn, an open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework, against universities in East Asia over about 48 hours starting Sept. 8. Given only target IP addresses and the goal "obtain shell access," the AI agents found a previously unknown path traversal flaw in an open-source medical imaging AI application and used it to get root access on one university server, then the same flaw was used to break into a second university.
- [Austrian Foreign Ministry website](https://hacktracking.com/#austrian-foreign-ministry-website-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Austria's foreign ministry says its website, run by an outside service provider, was accessed without authorization on Nov. 12-13, during the global Microsoft outage. It detected the intrusion on Nov. 13 and stopped it. The ministry announced it on Nov. 20.
- [Valley Family Health Care (community health center, Idaho and Oregon)](https://hacktracking.com/#valley-family-health-care-2026-03) (Mar 13, 2026, Medium): Valley Family Health Care, a Payette, Idaho-based community health center with clinics in southwestern Idaho and eastern Oregon, says it had a network disruption on or about March 13, 2026, and an investigation found that an unauthorized actor accessed and took certain files. It finished reviewing the files on Oct. 9 and began mailing notices on Nov. 18.
- [WOW WORLD (marketing communications service, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#wow-world-2026-11) (Nov 20, 2026, Low): Tokyo marketing-communications company WOW WORLD says a third party broke into some servers used to run its services and took out part of the client-company data stored on them. It blocked the access and is investigating how the attackers got in.
- [Bell Financial Group (stockbroker, Australia)](https://hacktracking.com/#bell-financial-group-2026-11) (Nov 20, 2026, Low): Bell Financial Group told the Australian stock exchange on Nov. 20 that there had been unauthorized access to a limited number of its IT systems, and that it believes some clients' data was accessed.
- [ui42 (web development agency, Slovakia; Dedoles)](https://hacktracking.com/#ui42-2026-11) (Nov 20, 2026, Low): Slovak digital agency ui42 says an attacker used a colleague's compromised login credentials to get into its internal systems, reached sensitive information from some client projects, including former client Dedoles, and then tried to extort the company.
- [Staples Canada (staplesprint.ca print website)](https://hacktracking.com/#staples-canada-2026-11) (Nov 1, 2026, Low): Staples Canada says an unknown party got unauthorized access to its staplesprint.ca website between Nov. 1 and Nov. 5 and had access to certain customer personal information. It told affected customers by email and says its other websites were not affected.
- [Atticus Administration (NYC retiree settlement claims database)](https://hacktracking.com/#atticus-administration-2026-09) (Sep 20, 2026, Low): An unknown user got into an online database run by Atticus Administration, a company hired to process settlement reimbursements for retired New York City government workers, on Sept. 20 and again periodically between Oct. 5 and 8, according to an Oct. 14 letter from Atticus's co-CEO to EmblemHealth that POLITICO obtained. Reimbursement submissions received on Oct. 12 were flagged as invalid, and EmblemHealth suspects they were attempts at fraudulent payments.
- [European Commission HR system (Sysper)](https://hacktracking.com/#european-commission-hr-system-2026-10) (Oct 22, 2026, High): The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack on Sysper, the internal HR platform staff use for salary information, leave requests, timesheets and training sign-ups. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier called it an "AI-generated cyber campaign" first detected on Oct. 22. POLITICO reported that CERT-EU linked the attackers to ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform; the Commission has not named the tool.
- [Mastercard (via third-party provider)](https://hacktracking.com/#mastercard-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, High): Mastercard said it was recently informed of an incident at a third-party provider that exposed a limited amount of information from a subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program. The ransomware gang n0n, which also listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase, had listed Mastercard on its leak site and published a dataset after its ransom deadline passed.
- [SBC Medical Group (Shonan Beauty Clinic operator, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#sbc-medical-group-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): SBC Medical Group, which runs Shonan Beauty Clinic and other cosmetic and medical clinics in Japan, said attackers got into one of its customer databases after hammering the system from overseas with about 770,000 attempts overnight. It found the intrusion on Nov. 16 and cut the server off the network. Separately, attackers logged into the clinics' accounts on the outside booking service Tribeau (トリビュー) and took reservation data.
- [PocketChange (currency exchange kiosks and Pokepay, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#pocketchange-2026-10) (Oct 26, 2026, High): PocketChange, which runs airport and station kiosks that swap leftover foreign cash for e-money and gift codes, says attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party internal business system on Oct. 26, then broke into its operating systems on Nov. 13 and used stolen credentials to reach an old monitoring system of its Pokepay (Enterprise) e-money platform on Nov. 14.
- [VMware vCenter zero-day attacks (CVE-2026-123890)](https://hacktracking.com/#vmware-vcenter-zero-day-attacks-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, High): Broadcom patched a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass on Nov. 19. Google's Mandiant says a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) had been exploiting it as a zero-day since early September, after first breaking in through BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances.
- [DonorPerfect (nonprofit fundraising platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#donorperfect-2026-11) (Nov 10, 2026, High): DonorPerfect, owned by SofterWare, says it was hit by a sophisticated cyberattack that entered through its marketing website. Staff noticed anomalies the week of Nov. 3, and on the evening of Nov. 10 the company took the platform offline for its more than 11,000 nonprofit customers. Company president Lauren Sheehan said other fundraising platforms were attacked by the same actor in the same period.
- [Forest & Bird (conservation group, New Zealand)](https://hacktracking.com/#forest-bird-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): New Zealand environmental advocacy group Forest & Bird says hackers got into its systems and accessed supporters' details. It was alerted on the evening of Nov. 18, and a forensic search of its website found malicious files hidden there to read data.
- [KPMG Canada (accounting firm)](https://hacktracking.com/#kpmg-canada-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): KPMG Canada confirmed a data breach in which client tax documents were compromised, and is contacting affected clients. It is the latest in a string of breaches at Canadian professional services firms, including several big Bay Street law firms.
- [FFG Industries (Fukuoka Financial Group company, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#ffg-industries-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Medium): Fukuoka Bank said a third party gained unauthorized access to a data analysis tool used by FFG Industries, a Fukuoka Financial Group company, to compile data from its ordering systems. The tool was set up and run by an outside contractor, and some information in the database it connected to may have leaked.
- [Openlogi (shipping and fulfillment service, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#openlogi-2026-11) (Nov 8, 2026, Medium): An outside party broke into systems at Openlogi, a Japanese warehouse and shipping service used by online stores, on Nov. 8-9 and took shipping data. Store clients including Kashima Antlers FC, United Arrows' overseas shops, REALITY Studios, Toei Animation's online lottery shop and Calpis's butter online shop have since warned their customers.
- [Atlas Confit (academic conference system, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#atlas-confit-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Atlas, which runs the Confit system that Japanese academic societies use for conferences, says an attacker abroad exploited a flaw in how one optional feature checked users and their permissions, likely found by scanning broadly for weaknesses with AI or similar tools, and pulled presenter information it should not have been able to see.
- [Greiz-Ronneburg district hospital (Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#greiz-ronneburg-district-hospital-2026-11) (Nov 14, 2026, Medium): A hacker attack on Kreiskrankenhaus Greiz-Ronneburg in Thuringia caused a system failure noticed on the evening of Nov. 14. The district says the hospital received an extortion message on Nov. 15 and calls the attack an extortion attempt.
- [Kosé (cosmetics maker, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#kos-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, Medium): Kosé says attackers abused an access-control flaw in the booking system for in-store experiences and lessons at its Maison KOSÉ Ginza and Omotesando shops, sending a rapid stream of requests on Nov. 9 to read members' personal data. On Nov. 19 it disclosed a second leak: customer data it kept in PLAID's KARTE marketing service was taken in the KARTE breach.
- [Ohio public libraries (Cuyahoga County, Akron-Summit County, Westlake Porter; via vendors)](https://hacktracking.com/#ohio-public-libraries-2026-11) (Nov 15, 2026, Medium): Three Northeast Ohio library systems say attackers got into patron account data through outside vendors that handle customer accounts, checkouts and room reservations. Cuyahoga County Public Library says the incident happened Nov. 15, was discovered the next day and is one of several affecting libraries and vendor systems across the country. The vendors have not been named.
- [Oneonta City School District (New York)](https://hacktracking.com/#oneonta-city-school-district-2026-10) (Oct 23, 2026, Medium): The Oneonta City School District closed schools for two days after a ransomware attack. An email account calling itself Shiba ransomware claimed the attack on Oct. 27 and threatened to publish records of students, parents and staff. In a Nov. 18 message, the superintendent said the forensic investigation is finished and investigators are now reviewing the data.
- [Southwire (wire and cable maker, employee health plan)](https://hacktracking.com/#southwire-2026-01) (Jan 29, 2026, Medium): Southwire, the Carrollton, Georgia, maker of electrical wire and cable, is notifying members of its employee health and welfare plan that an unauthorized third party had access to its computer systems between November 2025 and January 2026 and took files. It spotted the suspicious activity on Jan. 29, 2026.
- [Ochsner Health (Louisiana health system)](https://hacktracking.com/#ochsner-health-2026-09) (Sep 18, 2026, Medium): Louisiana's largest health provider said an "unauthorized actor" got into two employees' Microsoft accounts between Sept. 18 and Sept. 21 and downloaded files from one of them. Ochsner learned of it on Oct. 1 and hired a forensic firm.
- [Wilmington School District 209-U (Illinois)](https://hacktracking.com/#wilmington-school-district-209-u-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Superintendent Kevin Feeney told families the Will County district "experienced a ransomware attack that may have involved a data breach" on Nov. 17. The district suspended use of its laptops and other Windows devices as a precaution.
- [Kern Medical (hospital, Bakersfield, California)](https://hacktracking.com/#kern-medical-2026-09) (Sep 17, 2026, Low): Kern Medical, the public hospital run by the Kern County Hospital Authority, says it found unusual activity on Sept. 17 and that an unauthorized third party copied files with patient information. According to its breach notice as reported by HIPAA Journal, an attacker posing as IT staff phoned an employee and tricked them into changing their account login settings, then got into that employee's Microsoft 365 and storage account and copied data on Sept. 16–17. It announced the breach on Nov. 16.
- [Money Forward (fintech, Japan, via Notion and Fireworks AI)](https://hacktracking.com/#money-forward-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Low): Money Forward said some Notion AI chat records from three of its group companies may have leaked after hackers broke into Fireworks AI, the provider Notion used to process its AI features. Notion told the company on Nov. 10. Money Forward says its own services and systems were not accessed.
- [Kyash (payments app, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#kyash-2026-10) (Oct 28, 2026, Low): Kyash says an outsider got into one of its internal web tools for about two and a half hours on Oct. 28 because of an access-control flaw, and may have taken internal documents that included some customer information. It says the Kyash app and card systems were not accessed.
- [Steinberg (music software accounts)](https://hacktracking.com/#steinberg-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Low): Steinberg, maker of the Cubase music software, says attackers used email and password pairs likely leaked from other, unrelated breaches to break into a limited number of Steinberg accounts (credential stuffing).
- [USEN-ALMEX PreCheck-in (hotel online check-in service, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#usen-almex-precheck-in-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Low): USEN-ALMEX said attackers hit the system-integration API of PreCheck-in, its online pre-check-in service for hotels, with continuous access starting Nov. 14. It found the unauthorized access on Nov. 15 and shut the service down on Nov. 16. Hotel operators using it, including Solare Hotels and Resorts, are notifying guests.
- [UCHealth (University of Colorado Health)](https://hacktracking.com/#uchealth-2026-07) (Jul 27, 2026, Low): UCHealth, the nonprofit health system based in Aurora, Colorado, said someone got into two employee email accounts in Microsoft's cloud. Suspicious activity was found on July 27, 2026; it announced the breach in November.
- [Expedia Group (travel)](https://hacktracking.com/#expedia-group-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Critical): Expedia Group, owner of Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo, confirmed attackers reached its systems through a compromised third-party data platform provider in a supply chain attack that hit several companies. The n0n extortion group claims it stole more than 1 TB of Expedia data. Security researchers had described a similar attack using access tied to the Qubole data platform; Expedia has not named the vendor. On Nov. 18 Expedia told The Seattle Times it was investigating, calling n0n's data claims "unverified claims from criminals," and said its platforms remain safe to use.
- [Optimizely (website experimentation platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#optimizely-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Critical): Attackers exploited a flaw in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into scripts that run on customers' websites. Researchers at Report URI found the code on 178 organizations' sites, including big names like Salesforce, Zoom, HSBC, CNN and Ikea, so visitors to those sites were exposed without the companies themselves being breached.
- [Irish credit unions (via Wellington IT)](https://hacktracking.com/#irish-credit-unions-2026-10) (Oct 6, 2026, High): An attacker exploited a flaw in the online banking platform Wellington IT provides to Irish credit unions and pulled saved payee records in early October. Credit unions were only told in mid-November.
- [PayU Payments (payment firm, India)](https://hacktracking.com/#payu-payments-2026-11) (Nov 5, 2026, High): Gurugram police say attackers got into three cloud servers of payments company PayU on the night of Nov. 5–6, ran scripts that manipulated its payout system, registered 156 bank accounts as beneficiaries and moved about ₹25.67 crore out of its escrow account in 265 unauthorized payments. PayU filed a police complaint on Nov. 9.
- [Mercado Bitcoin (crypto exchange, Brazil)](https://hacktracking.com/#mercado-bitcoin-2026-11) (Nov 2, 2026, High): An attacker drained hot wallets at Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, in the early hours of Nov. 2, moving assets across multiple blockchains. On-chain investigators at Auditkey say the transfers were signed by the exchange's own wallets and did not involve a smart contract flaw; they call a compromise of keys or the signing system a possibility, not a conclusion.
- [Municipality of Neuried (Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#municipality-of-neuried-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Police say unknown attackers got into parts of the IT systems of Neuried, a town in Baden-Württemberg, and left a message there. The mayor discovered the attack on Nov. 17 and the affected systems were shut down as a precaution.
- [Perry Local Schools (Stark County, Ohio)](https://hacktracking.com/#perry-local-schools-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): A cyber incident knocked out the district's communications systems and much of its technology, including phones and internet access, and forced all Perry Local buildings to close on Monday, Nov. 16. On Nov. 18 the district said its investigation found malware caused the incident.
- [Mitsui Shopping Park app (Mitsui Fudosan, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#mitsui-shopping-park-app-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Mitsui Fudosan and Mitsui Fudosan Retail Management said a third party gained unauthorized access to the Mitsui Shopping Park app and leaked part of its point-program member data. They found the access on Nov. 18 and suspended the app the same day.
- [Wittenberg-Net (regional internet provider, Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#wittenberg-net-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Stadtwerke Wittenberg confirmed that criminals attacked the systems of its regional internet and phone provider Wittenberg-Net overnight into Wednesday, Nov. 18, causing a widespread outage around Wittenberg in Saxony-Anhalt. All relevant systems were taken offline as a precaution.
- [Star Petroleum Refining (SPRC, Thailand)](https://hacktracking.com/#star-petroleum-refining-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Thai oil refiner Star Petroleum Refining told the Stock Exchange of Thailand it was hit by a cyberattack that gave attackers unauthorized access to company data.
- [StubHub International (ticket resale)](https://hacktracking.com/#stubhub-international-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): StubHub International, the non-U.S. ticket resale business run by Ticketbis, told customers it detected unauthorized access to certain systems between late October and early November.
- [Ethiopian Airlines](https://hacktracking.com/#ethiopian-airlines-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Ethiopian Airlines emailed members of its ShebaMiles frequent-flyer program warning that some customer information may have been exposed in a recent cyberattack it called "of limited scope."
- [Infoblox (network security company)](https://hacktracking.com/#infoblox-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): The networking and security company confirmed hackers accessed company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.
- [Scattered Spider phishing and SIM-swap ring (Tyler Buchanan sentenced)](https://hacktracking.com/#scattered-spider-phishing-and-sim-swap-ring-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Tyler Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, was sentenced on Nov. 17 by a federal judge in Santa Ana, California, to six years in prison. From September 2021 to April 2023 he and co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen tech, telecom and crypto companies, used stolen logins to get into company systems, and then used SIM swaps to break into individuals' crypto accounts. He is the last of five defendants in the case, which has been linked to the Scattered Spider hacking group.
- [Hospital Clínico Universidad de Chile (hospital, Santiago)](https://hacktracking.com/#hospital-cl-nico-universidad-de-chile-2026-11) (Nov 14, 2026, Medium): The University of Chile's teaching hospital says it has been dealing with a cybersecurity incident since the morning of Saturday, Nov. 14 that knocked out part of its institutional computer systems. Its IT team activated containment protocols and is working with Chile's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCI) and the university's IT office to restore systems safely.
- [Klinik im Kurpark (hospital, Bad Rothenfelde, Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#klinik-im-kurpark-2026-11) (Nov 2, 2026, Low): The Klinik im Kurpark in Bad Rothenfelde, Lower Saxony, shut down its computer systems after a data incident reported to management on Monday, Nov. 2, and staff worked with pen and paper for ten days. The clinic's managing director told NDR the malware apparently got in through an external service provider and that a hired firm attributes the attack to a relatively new hacker group from China.
- [Nitori (furniture retailer, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#nitori-2026-11) (Nov 6, 2026, High): Japan's biggest furniture chain found intruders in a company system and says customer and order records may have been stolen.
- [accesso ticketing system (LEGOLAND Korea Resort and SEA LIFE Busan)](https://hacktracking.com/#accesso-ticketing-system-2026-11) (Nov 14, 2026, Medium): An outsider got into the ticketing system run by accesso, the reservation vendor for LEGOLAND Korea Resort and SEA LIFE Busan Aquarium, on Nov. 14 by exploiting a weakness, and looked up some annual pass holders' details. Both attractions posted notices on Nov. 16 warning customers their data may have leaked.
- [Japan health ministry drug supply system](https://hacktracking.com/#japan-health-ministry-drug-supply-system-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare said NTT Data, which runs and maintains its system for tracking drug supply shortages, reported unauthorized access by a third party. Traces show some stored data was viewed and someone tried to alter it, and a suspicious file was uploaded to the reporting system.
- [SOFT99 (car care products, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#soft99-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Low): Unauthorized access to an outside company that handles SOFT99's online-shop orders and shipping leaked customer order information.
- [Wilmington School District 209U (Illinois)](https://hacktracking.com/#wilmington-school-district-209u-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Low): The district's superintendent told families the district was hit by a ransomware attack that may have involved a data breach.
- [International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) website](https://hacktracking.com/#international-ice-hockey-federation-website-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Low): Hackers replaced the IIHF's homepage with a pro-Russian image and message criticizing Russia's exclusion from international competition. The image was reportedly up for several minutes before the site was taken offline.
- [South Korea government email system](https://hacktracking.com/#south-korea-government-email-system-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): South Korea's Ministry of the Interior and Safety said hackers got into the government's administrative email system by going through vulnerable local government networks and exploiting a flaw in its single sign-on (SSO) login system.
- [8-Digits Team ransomware group (extradition from Italy)](https://hacktracking.com/#8-digits-team-ransomware-group-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): The U.S. Justice Department said Roman Khlynovskiy, 43, a Kazakh national, was extradited from Italy and appeared in federal court in Knoxville, Tennessee, charged over his alleged role in the “8-Digits Team,” a group affiliated with the INC and Lynx ransomware that broke into networks of U.S. schools, hospitals and healthcare providers, stole data and demanded payment not to release it.
- [N-able N-central servers (zero-day attacks)](https://hacktracking.com/#n-able-n-central-servers-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, High): After a researcher published proof-of-concept exploits for more than 30 unpatched flaws in N-able's N-central remote management software, N-able took its hosted N-central environments offline on Nov. 9 and rushed out hotfixes. Attackers then exploited a newer flaw chain, 4EverAble2Shell, to get root access on exposed servers; N-able confirmed it is being used against customers who had not turned off the Legacy API.
- [Lithuanian Customs (user portal)](https://hacktracking.com/#lithuanian-customs-2026-11) (Nov 10, 2026, Medium): Lithuania's customs agency says attackers gained unauthorized access to BAP, the portal people and businesses use to log in to customs and some European Commission customs systems. It shut the portal down after detecting the attack on Nov. 10. Its chief called it a targeted, sophisticated attack that tried to go deeper into more sensitive systems.
- [Lighter (crypto exchange)](https://hacktracking.com/#lighter-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): An attacker drained funds from market-maker accounts on Lighter, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange, after the accounts' API keys were exposed. Lighter says the affected accounts used signing code outside its official software kits that reused cryptographic nonces, letting the attacker rebuild private keys from public signatures and move funds out through a public pool.
- [Transport for London (Oyster photocards)](https://hacktracking.com/#transport-for-london-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): Transport for London said it spotted suspicious activity on its Oyster photocard website on Nov. 16, after photocard holders got unexpected emails asking them to create an account they already had. It took the photocard system offline and says unauthorized access to customers' web account details resulted.
- [Wieson Technologies (connector maker, Taiwan)](https://hacktracking.com/#wieson-technologies-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Low): Wieson Technologies says it discovered on Nov. 16 that some of its information system servers had been hit by a cyberattack, and it isolated the affected servers and network equipment.
- [Coles Group (supermarkets, Australia)](https://hacktracking.com/#coles-group-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Low): Coles disclosed a cyber security incident in an ASX filing and said it is working with global cyber security experts to contain and secure its IT environment. It has not said what happened.
- [Jeonbuk Office of Education school bus system (South Korea)](https://hacktracking.com/#jeonbuk-office-of-education-school-bus-system-2026-11) (Nov 15, 2026, Low): South Korea's Jeonbuk provincial education office said its school bus management system was hacked on the evening of Nov. 15. It learned of the leak after being alerted by the Ministry of Education's cyber safety center, shut the system down and asked police to investigate.
- [Nikkei (via PLAID KARTE marketing service)](https://hacktracking.com/#nikkei-2026-11) (Nov 15, 2026, Low): KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that Nikkei uses, was accessed without authorization, and some Nikkei Online Edition user data it handled may have leaked.
- [Cursor (code editor, via Fireworks AI)](https://hacktracking.com/#cursor-2026-10) (Oct 29, 2026, Medium): Cursor said attackers used an access key stolen from its provider Fireworks AI to copy stored data, then used credentials found in that data to get into other internal systems. On Oct. 29 they used a stolen credential to put malicious copies of a popular extension on Cursor's extension marketplace for about 11 hours.
- [DHC (cosmetics, Japan, via PLAID KARTE)](https://hacktracking.com/#dhc-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, Critical): Unauthorized access to KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that DHC used for direct mail and similar messages, leaked DHC customer account information linked to it. PLAID notified DHC on Nov. 13.
- [Amadeus booking system (via Norwegian, Widerøe, SAS)](https://hacktracking.com/#amadeus-booking-system-2026-10) (Oct 27, 2026, High): Spanish travel booking platform Amadeus reported a security incident in which an unauthorized actor had access to its systems for at least three years, Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) says. Amadeus says a vulnerability in its booking display system made certain booking data accessible; it was closed on Sept. 23, 2026. The breach became known in Norway on Oct. 27.
- [Quantum Systems (military drone maker, Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#quantum-systems-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, High): Quantum Systems, which builds reconnaissance drones used by Germany's military and Ukraine, said it found an active cyberattack by hostile actors at the end of October. According to Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, attackers planted a malicious file disguised as an update to its QBase mission-planning software on the company's update server; it reached some customer servers, including German military ones, but not the drones.
- [City of Columbia (South Carolina)](https://hacktracking.com/#city-of-columbia-2026-10) (Oct 20, 2026, Medium): The city of Columbia found suspicious activity on its network on Oct. 20 and later confirmed it was a ransomware attack that hit several public-facing services and involved sensitive data on the city's network.
- [Dexcom (glucose monitor maker)](https://hacktracking.com/#dexcom-2026-11) (Nov 2, 2026, Medium): Dexcom, the U.S. maker of continuous glucose monitors, says an unauthorized third party used social engineering to get into certain employee accounts and download files. It determined on Nov. 2 that customers' information may have been involved and began notifying people on Nov. 13.
- [TSMC (chipmaker, Taiwan; employee data via cloud provider)](https://hacktracking.com/#tsmc-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company told the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that data on current and former employees was stolen from one of its cloud service providers. The filing came after a hacker offered 6.9 GB of alleged TSMC employee data for sale on a cybercrime forum on Nov. 8.
- [OPEN Inc. BizRobo! mini (automation software, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#open-inc-bizrobo-mini-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): An outside party got into the cloud environment that OPEN Inc. uses to run some of its services on Nov. 12, including the authentication server for its BizRobo! mini automation product. The company spotted a security alert on Nov. 16.
- [Lyko (beauty retailer, Sweden)](https://hacktracking.com/#lyko-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Unauthorized parties got into a small, isolated part of Swedish beauty retailer Lyko's systems and accessed customer data. Lyko says it stopped the breach within an hour and fixed the security hole.
- [Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre (hospital, Toronto)](https://hacktracking.com/#sunnybrook-health-sciences-centre-2026-10) (Oct 29, 2026, Medium): Sunnybrook, a major Toronto hospital, says unauthorized individuals accessed part of its network on Oct. 29 and that data, including some personal health information, was stolen.
- [Coinigy (crypto trading platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#coinigy-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Crypto trading platform Coinigy said it confirmed that an unauthorized party accessed its systems on the morning of Nov. 12, and that exchange API keys and secrets customers had stored on the platform may have been compromised. It took the service offline for a forensic investigation.
- [Rakuten Securities (online brokerage, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#rakuten-securities-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, Critical): Attackers got into a test-environment system at Rakuten Securities on Nov. 11 and customer data held there may have been taken. The company detected the intrusion on Nov. 16 and blocked it.
- [Maersk (shipping)](https://hacktracking.com/#maersk-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, High): The shipping giant confirmed that a threat actor breached a legacy system belonging to a company it previously acquired and stole data. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claimed the attack and threatened to release about 100GB of data, demanding $5 million (attacker's claim).
- [Meetsmore (service booking platform, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#meetsmore-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, Medium): Attackers logged into 201 accounts using passwords stolen elsewhere, then exploited a flaw in a scheduling feature to pull customer job details.

- [Front Systems (retail software, EG subsidiary)](https://hacktracking.com/#front-systems-2026-11) (Nov 5, 2026, Low): Software group EG says an unauthorized party got into Front Systems, retail software owned by its subsidiary Front Systems AS, on the evening of Nov. 5 and had access for about four hours. The attacker extracted about 0.2% of the Front Systems production database before access was closed.
- [French supermarket refrigeration systems (700+ stores)](https://hacktracking.com/#french-supermarket-refrigeration-systems-2026-10) (Oct 11, 2026, High): On Oct. 11 and 12, attackers took over the remote controls of refrigeration systems at more than 700 retail sites in France, pushing fridges and freezers into abnormal, indefinite defrost cycles and switching off temperature alarms. France has blamed Iran.
- [Vanderbilt University](https://hacktracking.com/#vanderbilt-university-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, High): Vanderbilt University in Nashville said on Nov. 9 it was responding to an active cyberattack affecting university devices, systems and cloud-based services, and told everyone to shut down university devices and get off campus Wi-Fi. The BYOD ransomware gang has claimed the attack; that claim has not been confirmed by the university.
- [University Hospitals (Cleveland health system)](https://hacktracking.com/#university-hospitals-2026-10) (Oct 22, 2026, High): University Hospitals in northeast Ohio says it detected unusual activity on its servers on Oct. 22 and disconnected its systems from the internet as a precaution. - [Apify (web scraping platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#apify-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, Medium): Apify, a Czech web scraping and browser automation platform, said an unauthorized third party got into parts of its internal systems on Nov. 9-10. It cut off the access, rotated internal secrets and API tokens, reset all sessions and revoked some third-party OAuth connections, including GitHub.
- [Trezor customers (via shipping partner Skladon)](https://hacktracking.com/#trezor-customers-2026-11) (Nov 7, 2026, Medium): Crypto hardware wallet maker Trezor says its shipping partner Skladon had unauthorized access to its systems on Nov. 7, and the attacker exported Trezor customer shipping data. Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15.
- [Port of Santos authority (Brazil)](https://hacktracking.com/#port-of-santos-authority-2026-11) (Nov 6, 2026, High): A cyberattack hit the Santos Port Authority (APS), the state-owned company that runs Brazil's largest port, knocking its online systems partly offline after a power outage at its headquarters. APS later confirmed a ransom demand. Brazil's Federal Police are investigating.
- [M1 (mobile carrier, Singapore)](https://hacktracking.com/#m1-2026-11) (Nov 6, 2026, Medium): Singapore mobile carrier M1 disclosed a data breach it identified on October 30 involving customer information. It says the breach has been contained.
- [Digital payments firm (Gurugram, India)](https://hacktracking.com/#digital-payments-firm-2026-11) (Nov 5, 2026, Medium): Hackers got into three cloud servers belonging to an unnamed Gurugram-based digital payments firm on the night of Nov. 5-6, ran malicious scripts and abused its payout API to send money out of its escrow account, police say. Two men from Ludhiana have been arrested.
- [Credit Mutuel Arkea (bank, France)](https://hacktracking.com/#credit-mutuel-arkea-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, Critical): Attackers got in through the platform of one of the bank's service providers and used Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's own account to send money to other banks, which was then converted into cryptocurrency. - [NTT Docomo (mobile carrier, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#ntt-docomo-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, High): NTT Docomo detected unauthorized outside access to its Docomo Online Shop and My docomo account site on Nov. 4 and shut down procedures on both early Nov. 5. The company later confirmed that some customer information was taken through the access.
- [2RedBeans (dating site)](https://hacktracking.com/#2redbeans-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, High): 2RedBeans (Embrace Inc.) said an unauthorized party got into one of its internal systems on Nov. 4 and copied member information before the access was detected and shut off on Nov. 5.
- [The Kyiv Independent (news outlet)](https://hacktracking.com/#the-kyiv-independent-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, Medium): Hackers got into the newsroom's website system and newsletter service, posting and emailing fake claims about Zelensky and Putin. The outlet suspects Russia.
- [SPH Media (news publisher, Singapore)](https://hacktracking.com/#sph-media-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, Medium): SPH Media, publisher of The Straits Times, found cyberattacks on five of its systems between Nov. 4 and Nov. 8, which it believes were carried out by the same threat actor.
